title: WCM conformance vendor-evidence vector v1
description: A conformance vector carrying a capture taken from real vendor silicon. The shape exists so a vector is about the vendor rather than about the file: the anchor is named and staged rather than carried, the binding it asserts is declared rather than assumed, and the refusal matrix is mandatory so a capture cannot arrive with only a happy path.

id.description: Unique across every kind, not only this one. The results contract keys on id alone, so two vectors sharing a name collapse into one scored entry.

expect.description: A vendor vector is a capture, and a capture is an accept. Its negatives are the refusal matrix, derived by the runner rather than contributed, which is what stops a capture arriving with only a happy path.

capture.description: Provenance. Without it a vector that starts failing is unattributable, and nobody can tell whether the implementation regressed or the platform moved.

part.description: The silicon, named as specifically as the platform allows.

tcb.description: Firmware or TCB level at capture time, where the platform reports one.

source.description: Where the capture was taken: the host, cloud, or machine.

evidence.description: The captured bytes, and nothing derived from them. There is nowhere here to record a digest of the report, and that absence is the pinning rule expressed in the schema rather than only in prose.

format.description: Selects the parser. An unrecognised format is a hard failure, never a skip.

chain.description: The anchor is named, never carried. A chain that supplies its own root proves only that the vector is internally consistent, which the synthetic PKI already proves.

root_source.description: Where a runner obtains this root. Documentation for a person, never a URL the runner fetches.

root_limit.description: A stated limit on this root, for the case where the vendor does not publish one in a form a runner can stage. Said here rather than left to the chain anchoring itself quietly.

binding.description: What REPORT_DATA is bound to, declared rather than assumed. Real captures do not uniformly echo a caller nonce, and a format with a bare nonce field invites an implementer to check the wrong thing and pass.

kind.description: nonce-digest: REPORT_DATA equals sha256(nonce). nonce-and-transport: sha256(nonce || transport key). nonce-echo: the nonce appears verbatim in the report at nonce_offset, rather than as a digest of it. attestation-key: bound to a platform key, no caller freshness. none: signature and chain only. An unrecognised kind is a hard failure, never a skip.

nonce_offset.description: Byte offset at which the report echoes the nonce verbatim. Belongs to nonce-echo alone: a kind that binds a digest has no offset to declare. A field rather than a constant, because a second platform echoing at a different offset should need a value and not a branch.

validity.description: The scored tier evaluates at now, so a score does not change as certificates age. not_after is the shortest-lived certificate the chain depends on, recorded so the horizon is visible without parsing chains and so the live tier has something to compare against.

refusals.description: The matrix, applied to every capture so a new capture cannot arrive with only a happy path. Each case names a substring the refusal reason must contain, never an exact message, or the vectors become a change detector for wording.
